headline: Margin rebound overshadowed by a big divestiture charge
summary_short: LyondellBasell's Q2 2026 revenue rose 19.8% y/y to $9.18 billion as diluted EPS jumped to $1.71 from $0.34, though an $842 million net-of-tax identified-items charge (mainly the completed European asset divestiture) cut EPS by $2.59; EPS excluding those items was $4.30.
summary_long: Revenue grew 19.8% y/y to $9.18B on expanding O&P-Americas margins and ~90% North American utilization amid tight global supply; O&P-EAI benefited from improved polymer spreads and stronger JV income, while I&D gained on oxyfuels/methanol/PO margins despite the (since-restarted) Bayport outage. GAAP net income of $558M and diluted EPS of $1.71 were held back by $842M of net-of-tax identified items, mainly the loss on the completed European O&P divestiture; excluding those, EPS was $4.30 and EBITDA $2.1B. Cash from operations was $752M; quarter-end cash was $2.63B with $7.1B total liquidity, aided by $310M of divestiture proceeds. Q3 guidance: 85% NA O&P, 70% EU O&P, 85% I&D operating rates; Cash Improvement Plan on track for its $500M FY2026 target.
